messages.subject: Using bquote with plyr
parts:
Hi,
I want to define a constant and then make that the default value for my input arguments, similar to the help via ?bquote. However, when I do that and my function has calls to plyr inside it, I run into problems with plyr's .() syntax, which is the same syntax bquote looks for. The below code demonstrates the issue and my proposed solution is in `bar2`. I figured I would post here in case I am missing something obvious or if anyone had any suggestions on how to still use `.` and `bquote`.

Thanks,
Doug

===

CONSTANT <- 6;
foo <- eval(bquote(function(f = .(CONSTANT)){ return(f); }));
foo()

bar <- eval(bquote(function(f = .(CONSTANT)){
library(plyr);
df <- data.frame(A = LETTERS[1:3], B = 1:3, stringsAsFactors = FALSE);
return(ddply(df, .(A)))
}))
## Errors

bar2 <- eval(bquote(function(f = .(CONSTANT)){
library(plyr);
df <- data.frame(A = LETTERS[1:3], B = 1:3, stringsAsFactors = FALSE);
return(ddply(df, "A")) # Use the "" syntax instead of `.`
}))
bar2()

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Using bquote with plyr
parts:
Hi Doug,

An alternative is to make the function by hand:

pryr::make_function(list(f = CONSTANT), quote({

library(plyr);
df <- data.frame(A = LETTERS[1:3], B = 1:3, stringsAsFactors = FALSE);

ddply(df, .(A))
}))

You can easily copy the contents of pryr::make_function locally if you
don't want to add a dependency to a non-cran package.

Hadley
